summary: Quarterly business review for Crestline Retail. Discussed usage trends (spike in conversational assistant traffic), rising token costs, latency SLO misses for peak hours, and roadmap alignment. Customer interested in Dedicated/reserved capacity and additional security artifacts. Agreed on follow-ups: pricing, benchmark, and security docs.
transcript:
00:00 Samir Patel: All right everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick roll call?
00:07 Maria Torres: Maria here, Head of ML Ops at Crestline. Jason is on as well.
00:10 Jason Liu: Hi all.
00:12 Priya Reddy: Priya from Redwood SE. Hey team.
00:15 Liam O'Connor: Liam, CSM. We'll keep this tight 45 minutes.
00:22 Samir Patel: Agenda: quick QBR metrics, cost trends, reliability/latency, security checklist, and next steps. Maria, do you want to start with how things are going from your side?
00:33 Maria Torres: Yeah thanks. So traffic has basically doubled in March-April, our shopping assistant usage went up with the spring promo. We're seeing a higher ratio of long context sessions, so token counts per request up 2x. Costs have spiked, that's our main pain.
00:48 Jason Liu: Also, around 3pm-5pm PST we've had latencies creep up; p95 for responses moved from 350ms to 700-900ms for the multi-turn flows. It's causing some UI timeouts.
01:02 Priya Reddy: Okay that's helpful. Do you know what model variants you're calling in those peaks, Maria? Are you on the standard hosted model or the quantized fast variants?
01:12 Maria Torres: Mostly the default redwood-large we set on prod last Q, we haven't switched to the q4 profiles. We wanted to get more data before changing quality.
01:21 Samir Patel: Right, and that's what we saw in usage reports. The higher token-per-session drives more per-token spend. There's also opportunity to enable prefix caching for your guided flows to reduce token re-generation.
01:33 Ben Carter: Quick note: we capture the first user turn on the client and send full context to Redwood, so maybe we can truncate some of that. But we still want model outputs consistent.
01:44 Priya Reddy: On the latency - two levers: batching and dedicated capacity. For your traffic shape, dedicated GPU pools with consistent throughput would remove noisy neighbor effects. We can also recommend batching profiles and KV/prefix cache.
01:58 Jason Liu: When you say dedicated, is that the Redwood Dedicated offering with reserved capacity and SLA? We need to justify cost.
02:06 Samir Patel: Yes, Redwood Dedicated - apologies if naming is slightly off in previous notes, I sometimes say 'Redwood Dedicate' - but it's the reserved capacity offering with a monthly commit and SLA. It typically lowers tail latency and unit cost for high-volume workloads.
02:20 Maria Torres: Can you give us ballpark numbers vs hosted? We need to compare the delta to justify committing.
02:26 Samir Patel: Ballpark: for steady high throughput workloads, Dedicated can reduce per-token cost 20-35% versus hosted peak pricing, depending on batch efficiency and model quantization. We will send a tailored quote.
02:39 Priya Reddy: We'll need sample traffic to run a sizing exercise. The benchmark will simulate your session length distribution and measure p50/p95 under steady and burst load.
02:49 Maria Torres: We can share anonymized logs, Ben will export.
02:51 Ben Carter: Yep exporting now, will share the S3 link.
02:55 Samir Patel: Great. On security: do you have any outstanding compliance asks beyond SOC2 and SSO?
03:02 Jason Liu: Data residency for EU is not an immediate need, but KMS integration and audit logs are required for our procurement to greenlight the contract. Also our legal asked about data retention and deletion scopes.
03:15 Liam O'Connor: We have the SOC2 report and the KMS integration guide; I'll attach them to the deal record. Audit logs for per-request tracing are available in Redwood Console, we can show the retention windows.
03:28 Priya Reddy: For KMS, our Private deployment supports customer-managed keys; Dedicated can also integrate with cloud KMS. We'll outline options in the tech doc.
03:38 Maria Torres: For the pilot, we want to run a 2-week dedicated benchmark, if the numbers look good we want to move to a 12-month reserved commit. Timeline is Q2 procurement.
03:50 Samir Patel: Sounds good. We'll scope the POC: 2-week dedicated run, baseline metrics (p95, token cost, error rate), and a rollback plan.
03:58 Jason Liu: On SLAs, what's the guaranteed p99? Our SRE asks for clear SLOs during business hours.
04:05 Priya Reddy: Our Dedicated SLA focuses on uptime and throughput; p99 latency guarantees depend on model and load profile. For the pilot we'll set target SLOs and measure them. We'll give a recommended runbook for graceful degradation - for example automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant under sustained overload.
04:24 Maria Torres: That's critical. We need automatic fallback; we had one incident where the assistant slowed and support tickets spiked.
04:33 Samir Patel: Noted. We can add a dual-model policy: primary high-quality model + fallback quantized model and automated routing in the event of capacity or latency breaches.
04:45 Ben Carter: Does that require code changes on our side or is it routing rules in Redwood Console?
04:51 Priya Reddy: Mostly routing rules and config changes. We can provide example A/B rollout and canary policies. Minimal SDK changes - usually just swap model id and a config flag.
05:02 Maria Torres: On costs, is there tooling to project monthly spend if we enable prefix caching and batching?
05:09 Liam O'Connor: Yes, Console has token-level cost breakdowns and per-route model dashboards. We can also run a simulated cost projection once you provide the traffic sample.
05:19 Samir Patel: A couple of notes from procurement: Crestline legal wants standard data processing addendum, and Bastion compliance will want to review encryption keys flow. We'll get those into cloudshare.
05:31 Jason Liu: Any competitors' gotchas we should know? We did a side-by-side with CloudCo and VertexAI; CloudCo's managed offering was cheaper but lacked the observability and fallback controls.
05:44 Priya Reddy: That's consistent; Redwood focuses on production controls and predictable economics.
05:50 Maria Torres: Roadmap asks from our side: better per-request tracing in Console UI, and more granular retention controls for audit logs. Also, can we get a feature flag to prefer cached responses for certain flows?
06:03 Priya Reddy: We have work in progress on enhanced tracing, and the cached response preference can be implemented via routing rules - we'll show a recipe. I'll add those to the action items.
06:15 Samir Patel: Ok let's recap and owners. Samir to send pricing and a reserved capacity sketch; Priya to schedule the deep technical sizing and run the pilot benchmarks; Ben to provide logs; Liam to attach SOC2 and SAML docs.
06:30 Maria Torres: Works for us. Any other open risks?
06:35 Jason Liu: Just procurement timing - we need numbers by first week of May to lock the Q2 budget.
06:41 Samir Patel: We'll prioritize that.
06:44 Speaker 1: (muttered) thanks everyone.
06:46 Samir Patel: Cool, we'll follow up in email and set the deep dive. Thanks all.
06:53 End of recording

Notes about transcript: occasional word swaps (e.g., 'Redwood Dedicate' for Dedicated), timestamps are approximate; some speaker labels are informal.
